headlineRule: These are two different claims and are reported separately on purpose. The owner instruction was: do not simulate hosted IPv6 and call it proof.

whatWasActuallyProvenHosted.claim: limiter.normalize_source executes correctly over IPv6 inputs on the real hosted Postgres 17 engine against the real staged catalog.
whatWasActuallyProvenHosted.negativeControlMeaning: A deliberately wrong expectation was included and was reported as a failure, so the 0 is a measurement, not a vacuous pass.
whatWasActuallyProvenHosted.residue: NONE — the suite ran inside one transaction that was never committed, and limiter.config was re-verified afterwards as ipv6_prefix=64, ipv4_prefix=32, window_seconds=86400, normal_allowance=5, bucket_allowance=50, enabled=true, require_public_ip=true.
coverage: RFC 4941-style privacy addresses in one /64 group to one bucket
a different /64 is a different bucket
host bits are zeroed (network(), not host()) — the defect that made /64 grouping never group
RFC 6052 well-known NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 unwraps to the embedded IPv4
RFC 8215 local-use NAT64 64:ff9b:1::/48 unwraps to the embedded IPv4
RFC 4291 IPv4-mapped ::ffff:0:0/96 unwraps to the embedded IPv4
two distinct NAT64 clients do NOT collapse into one bucket
a NAT64-embedded PRIVATE IPv4 is refused after unwrapping, not before
fe80::/10, fc00::/7, ::1, ff00::/8 and :: are all refused
a masked /64 input is refused as not a host address
comma-joined, whitespace-bearing, empty and malformed values are refused
uppercase/expanded and compressed spellings normalise identically
ipv6_prefix is genuine configuration: 128 separates two hosts in one /64, 48 widens grouping

reason1_noAAAAOnTheIngestHostname.measured: dig AAAA ctshxbykuemeqnofqcdh.supabase.co -> no records. Only A records (172.64.149.246, 104.18.38.10, Cloudflare).
reason1_noAAAAOnTheIngestHostname.consequence: No client anywhere can open an IPv6 connection to the staging API/Edge surface, because no AAAA is published for it. This is a property of the deployment, not of the test machine.

reason2_theTestMachineIsNotTheLimitation.measured: This host has working global IPv6 egress: curl -6 to one.one.one.one returned HTTP 200 from 2606:4700:4700::1001, and the host holds 4 global-scope IPv6 addresses.
reason2_theTestMachineIsNotTheLimitation.measured2: curl -6 to the staging host connected to ::ffff:104.18.38.10 — an IPv4-mapped socket, i.e. it fell back to the A record. The connection was IPv4.
reason2_theTestMachineIsNotTheLimitation.consequence: The inability to originate hosted IPv6 is not an environment excuse. IPv6 egress was demonstrated to a different host in the same test run.

reason3_noGuestIngestEdgeFunctionExists.fact: The accepted Phase 03A artifact set contains NO guest-ingest Edge Function. The three deployed functions are send-push-notification v6, notify-flag-status v8 and delete-account v4, none of which is a guest ingestion path.
reason3_noGuestIngestEdgeFunctionExists.consequence: Even over IPv4 there is currently no hosted code path that reads cf-connecting-ip and calls the limiter. End-to-end hosted ingestion — of any address family — cannot be proven in this run, and deploying an ad-hoc function to manufacture one is outside the accepted artifact set and outside this authorization.

productionRelevantFinding.reading: The client-facing API/Edge hostname is IPv4-only in DNS on BOTH staging and production. The direct database hostname is IPv6-only on both — but the limiter never observes the database connection's peer address, so that is irrelevant to guest admission.
productionRelevantFinding.implication: As DNS is published today, an IPv6-only client reaches this deployment through DNS64/NAT64 or 464XLAT, so Cloudflare — and therefore cf-connecting-ip — sees an IPv4 address. The IPv6 normalization paths are DORMANT in production rather than load-bearing.
productionRelevantFinding.whyItStillMatters: Dormant is not dead. If Supabase or Cloudflare later publishes an AAAA for the API hostname, cf-connecting-ip begins carrying IPv6 with no code change and no deploy. The /64 grouping then becomes load-bearing overnight. That is exactly why the normalization is proven now rather than deferred.
productionRelevantFinding.claimBound: Bounded to DNS as published on 2026-09-10 and to a read-only DNS lookup. No production request was made, no production record was read, and no production object was touched.

howToCloseItLater: Closing HOSTED_IPV6_TRANSPORT requires two things this authorization does not grant: (a) a guest-ingest Edge Function in the accepted artifact set, and (b) an IPv6-reachable ingest hostname. Until both exist, the honest status is OPEN, and it must not be reported as PASS on the strength of the normalization result above.
privacyDiscipline: Every address used in the assertions is an RFC 3849 (2001:db8::/32) or RFC 5737 (203.0.113.0/24) documentation sentinel, or a well-known reserved prefix. No real client address was captured, stored, logged or reasoned about.
